scope: Bounded discovery of Maltese legislation and reuse, EU/EEA/Swiss free movement and family routes, distinct UK Withdrawal Agreement and third-country-sponsor procedures, visa and consular practice, procedural/appeal review, public access, privacy, oversight, legal aid, civil-status evidence and court-search routes. This is not a complete inventory or legal-equivalence opinion.

comparison_seed.source: Danish EU free-movement residence regulation and official guidance
comparison_seed.relationship_note: Maltese S.L. 460.17 and Identità procedures have a close functional relationship to the Danish EU-residence seed, but Malta has its own statutory definitions, registration procedure and Immigration Appeals Board. EEA EFTA, Swiss, mobile-Maltese, third-country-sponsor and UK Withdrawal Agreement routes must be separately established; no legal equivalence is asserted.

previous_findings_carried_forward: Use author-source-pack-rules cross-state discovery as a topic/source seed, not as evidence that Malta has an equivalent instrument; verify each candidate at the responsible first-party publisher.

Carry forward the sustainability rule: API/ELI documentation, stable-looking identifiers and an open-data law do not prove live access, record coverage, rights to reuse, currentness or conversion behavior.

Carry forward prior Greece and Hungary findings: inspect reuse terms and access limits for the exact publisher endpoint before automated copying/conversion; do not transfer another jurisdiction’s license conclusion.

Carry forward prior Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania and Luxembourg findings: compare current source pages and attachment versions with primary legislative amendment records; stale guidance indices and mutable PDFs need parent-page rediscovery.

Search legal records, operational guidance/forms, visa and mission practice, remedies, public access, civil status, privacy, oversight, legal aid and case law separately. N-Lex is a legal discovery lead, not a complete source inventory.
Keep the EU free-movement, EEA EFTA, Swiss bilateral, mobile-Maltese family and UK Withdrawal Agreement categories distinct unless Maltese primary law proves their scope.
